title: Develop ideas before polishing conventions
statement: Where a writing rubric gives an undeveloped response no credit for conventions, teach learners to develop and organise ideas before polishing conventions.
example: In one state test's Grade 3 essay rubric, scored 0 to 3 for development and 0 to 2 for conventions, a 0 for development forces a 0 for conventions.
detail: A research report on a state reading test's Grade 3 writing task, kept in a reading course's documentation, quotes the scoring guide's interaction rule: a response scored 0 for development and organisation of ideas also earns 0 for conventions (`othello-course-renderer-draft/repo/docs/extras/alpharead-staar-writing-research.md`, line 102). The course's Grade 3 writing scaffold, grounded in that report, makes development the gatekeeper: build ideas first, conventions last (`othello-course-renderer-draft/repo/docs/extras/alpharead-writing-scaffold-overview.md`, line 20). The order follows from how that rubric scores, and nothing here measured what teaching in this order does.
against: The rule runs one way only: the same report notes that a fully developed essay can still earn 0 for conventions if it is one long run-on (`othello-course-renderer-draft/repo/docs/extras/alpharead-staar-writing-research.md`, line 104), so conventions still need teaching once ideas are developed. The rubric is one state's, and the report calls itself Texas-specific (line 12).

evidence.quote: > "…if a response receives a score point 0 in the Development and Organization of Ideas trait, the response will also earn 0 points in the Conventions trait."
Development & Organization of Ideas (0–3) + Conventions (0–2) = 0–5 per scorer
with **Development as the gatekeeper** — build ideas first, conventions last.
a fully developed essay (Dev 3) can still earn Conventions 0 if it's one giant run-on
if a response receives a score point 0 in the Development and Organization of Ideas trait, the response will also earn 0 points in the Conventions trait.

The reverse is not true: a fully developed essay (Dev 3) can still earn Conventions 0 if it's one giant run-on; a thin essay (Dev 1) can earn Conventions 2 if clean. **Development is the gatekeeper.**

Grounded in the Grade 3 STAAR RLA research: the essay rewards **Development & Organisation of Ideas (0–3) + Conventions (0–2)**, with **Development as the gatekeeper** — build ideas first, conventions last.

citations.ref: Texas Education Agency 2025, STAAR Grade 3 RLA Constructed-Response Scoring Guide, Spring 2025
